concerns.text: Success Criterion SC-001 requires detecting an effect (Cohen’s d ≥ 0.3 with p < 0.05 in ≥ 80 % of bootstrap resamples) for the project to be considered successful. This ties the project’s success to a positive finding, making a null result a failure and creating a circular validation of the hypothesis.

Success Criterion SC-002 demands that all strata achieve p < 0.05 and a coefficient‑of‑variation < 0.1. This again makes statistical significance a prerequisite for project success, biasing the study toward confirming the hypothesis and preventing a rigorous null‑result report.

SC-003 requires reporting the stability of anomaly detection across σ thresholds, but the specification only mentions sweeping thresholds (FR‑007) without stating that variation in significance rates or inconsistency rates will be measured and reported as required.

The provided Monte‑Carlo power simulation shows only 0.68 power for a medium effect (Cohen’s d≈0.5), below the conventional 0.80 target. With such low power the study is at high risk of a false‑negative conclusion, undermining the scientific validity of the investigation.

Control windows are matched only on ENSO and PDO indices. Important confounders such as local temperature, humidity, and finer‑scale pressure cycles are omitted, which could bias the comparison between event and control windows.

The two‑sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test assumes independent observations. Even with 30‑day event‑thinning, spatial and temporal autocorrelation likely remain, violating the independence assumption and inflating Type I error.

The left‑censored 30‑day moving average baseline includes a 12‑day gap before the event. If precursory signals have longer lead times, this baseline may still leak signal, contaminating the anomaly calculation. No sensitivity analysis on gap length is specified.

Applying Benjamini‑Hochberg correction across all strata dramatically reduces power. The plan does not pre‑specify a limited set of primary hypotheses or employ hierarchical testing to balance false‑discovery control with sensitivity.

The NOAA NCEP/NCAR reanalysis dataset is accessed via an OPeNDAP endpoint that is not listed in the Verified Datasets block, violating Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) and casting doubt on the scientific reliability of the primary data source.
